newsitem.title: FINLAND: PULP OPTIONS TRADE TO START FEB 4 - FINNISH EXCHANGE.
newsitem.headline: PULP OPTIONS TRADE TO START FEB 4 - FINNISH EXCHANGE.

text.p: Suomen Optioporssi Oy , a Finnish options exchange, said in a statement on Monday that trade in its pulp derivatives would start on February 4.
"Trading in the pulp options and futures contract will commence on February 4, 1997 at noon," SOP said.
"Trading will begin with options and futures on Northern Bleached Softwood Kraft (NBSK) with expiration on March 24 and June 30, 1997," it added.
Initially there will be a two-month and a five-month contract. Contract settlement will always be in cash based upon the PIX pulp price index. No physical delivery is possible.
SOP said it had been notified by 22 companies that they will participate in trading. Of these, 11 have applied for a direct account with the exchange.

SOP's pulp options and futures -- which treat pulp as a commodity based on SOP's own pulp price benchmark index -- can be used by the forest industry and its clients to hedge against pulp price fluctuation.
Since last autumn, SOP has published every Monday the value of its northern bleached softwood pulp index (PIX). Last Monday, it was $558.70 per tonne, up from $557.47 the previous week.
Information for calculation of the benchmark pulp price is supplied by more than 30 companies from 11 different countries.
In December, the PIX mean was $559.05, down from $564.54 in November.
